subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “The children almost ate the whole cake before the guests arrived.”
o: The children eat almost the whole cake before the guests arrived.
The children almost ate the whole cake before the guests arrived.
The children ate almost the whole cake before the guests arrived.
The children ate almost the whole cake before the guests arrive.
explanation: “Almost” should qualify “the whole cake”; placed before “ate”, it says they nearly ate but did not eat at all.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “It is high time the government takes notice of the water crisis.”?
o: It is high time the government took notice on the water crisis.
It is high time the government took notice of the water crisis.
It is high time the government takes notice of the water crisis.
It is high time the government has taken notice of the water crisis.
explanation: After “it is high time”, English uses the past tense (“took”) to refer to the present; one takes notice “of” something.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “I wish I studied harder before the preliminary test last year.”
o: I wish I had studied harder before a preliminary test last year.
I wish I had studied more harder before the preliminary test last year.
I wish I studied harder before the preliminary test last year.
I wish I had studied harder before the preliminary test last year.
explanation: A wish about the past takes the past perfect (“had studied”); “more harder” is a double comparative.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “The police has arrested three suspects near the border.”
o: The police have arrested three suspects near the border.
The police have arrest three suspects near the border.
The polices have arrested three suspects near the border.
The police has arrested three suspects near the border.
explanation: “Police” is a plural noun without an -s form, so it takes “have”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “Indus is the longest river in Pakistan.”?
o: Indus is the longest river in Pakistan.
The Indus is the most longest river in Pakistan.
The Indus is the longest river in Pakistan.
The Indus is a longest river in Pakistan.
explanation: Names of rivers take “the”; a superlative takes “the” and cannot be combined with “most”.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The former mayor was accused for corruption and misuse of funds.”?
o: The former mayor was accuse of corruption and misuse of funds.
The former mayor was accused of corruption and misuse of funds.
The former mayor were accused of corruption and misuse of funds.
The former mayor was accused for corruption and misuse of funds.
explanation: A person is “accused of” an offence; the singular subject needs “was” and the passive needs the participle “accused”.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “A good manager knows how to plan, organise and the leading of a team.”
o: A good manager knows how to plan, organise and the leading of a team.
A good manager knows how to plan, organise and lead a team.
A good manager know how to plan, organise and lead a team.
A good manager knows how to plan, organise and lead an team.
explanation: The three verbs after “how to” must share the base form: “plan, organise and lead”.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “Many experts believe this variety of cotton is superior than the old one.”
o: Many experts believe this variety of cotton is more superior to the old one.
Many expert believe this variety of cotton is superior to the old one.
Many experts believe this variety of cotton is superior to the old one.
Many experts believe this variety of cotton is superior than the old one.
explanation: “Superior” is a Latin comparative: it takes “to” and is never preceded by “more”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “Although the road was narrow, but the driver kept a steady speed.”?
o: Although the road was narrow, the driver kept a steady speed.
Although the road was narrow, but the driver kept a steady speed.
Although the road were narrow, the driver kept a steady speed.
Although the road was narrow, the driver keeps a steady speed yesterday.
explanation: “Although” already links the clauses, so adding “but” is redundant.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The farmer who’s crops were destroyed has received compensation.”?
o: The farmer whose crops were destroyed have received compensation.
The farmer whose crops was destroyed has received compensation.
The farmer who’s crops were destroyed has received compensation.
The farmer whose crops were destroyed has received compensation.
explanation: “Whose” is the possessive relative pronoun, while “who’s” means “who is”; “crops” takes “were” and “farmer” takes “has”.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “Hardly had the plane landed than the passengers began to stand.”
o: Hardly had the plane land when the passengers began to stand.
Hardly the plane had landed when the passengers began to stand.
Hardly had the plane landed than the passengers began to stand.
Hardly had the plane landed when the passengers began to stand.
explanation: “Hardly” is completed by “when” (not “than”) and requires inverted word order with the past perfect.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “The cattle is grazing in the fields near the canal.”
o: The cattle are grazing at the fields near the canal.
The cattles are grazing in the fields near the canal.
The cattle are grazing in the fields near the canal.
The cattle is grazing in the fields near the canal.
explanation: “Cattle” is a plural noun with no -s form, so it takes “are”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “My teacher gave me an useful advice about the interview.”?
o: My teacher gave me a useful piece of advice about the interview.
My teacher gave me an useful advice about the interview.
My teacher gave me a useful piece of advise about the interview.
My teacher gave me a useful advices about the interview.
explanation: “Advice” is uncountable, so it cannot take “a/an” or a plural; “a piece of advice” counts it. “Gave me” needs no “to”.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The final report was quite different than the draft we saw.”?
o: The final report were quite different from the draft we saw.
The final report was quite different from the draft we saw.
The final report was quite different to the draft we seen.
The final report was quite difference from the draft we saw.
explanation: The standard form is “different from”; the other options contain errors of agreement, verb form (“we seen”) and part of speech (“difference”).

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “The guard did not let him to enter the building without a pass.”
o: The guard did not let him enter into the building without a pass.
The guard did not let him to enter the building without a pass.
The guard did not let he enter the building without a pass.
The guard did not let him enter the building without a pass.
explanation: “Let” is followed by an object and a bare infinitive; “enter” takes a direct object without “into” in this sense.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “Unless you do not register by Monday, you cannot sit the test.”
o: Unless you register by Monday, you cannot sit the test.
Unless you will register by Monday, you cannot sit the test.
Unless you do not register by Monday, you cannot sit the test.
Unless you register until Monday, you cannot sit the test.
explanation: “Unless” already means “if not”, so another “not” reverses the meaning; a deadline takes “by”, not “until”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “A lot of people was waiting outside the passport office.”?
o: A lot of people was waiting outside the passport office.
A lot of peoples were waiting outside the passport office.
A lot of people were waiting outside the passport office.
A lot of people were waiting outside the passport office since morning.
explanation: With “a lot of”, the verb agrees with the noun that follows; “people” is plural, so “were” is correct.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “He promised that he will send the documents the next day.”?
o: He promised that he will send the documents the next day.
He promised that he would send the documents the next day.
He promised that he would sent the documents the next day.
He promised that he would send the document’s the next day.
explanation: After a past reporting verb, “will” shifts to “would”; “would” takes the base verb.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “To improve public health, more clinics are needed by the province.”
o: To improve public health, the province needs more clinics.
To improve public health, more clinics are needed by the province.
To improving public health, the province needs more clinics.
To improve public health, the province need more clinics.
explanation: An introductory infinitive phrase must refer to the subject that performs it, so “the province” should be the subject.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “The principal gave we students permission to leave early.”
o: The principal gave us students permission for leave early.
The principal given us students permission to leave early.
The principal gave we students permission to leave early.
The principal gave us students permission to leave early.
explanation: The pronoun is an object of “gave”, so “us students” is correct.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “Ahmed is elder than his cousin by three years.”?
o: Ahmed is more older than his cousin by three years.
Ahmed is elder than his cousin by three years.
Ahmed is older than his cousin by three years.
Ahmed is older then his cousin by three years.
explanation: “Elder” is not followed by “than”; the comparative for age in a “than” comparison is “older”.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The delegation arrived to the airport late at night.”?
o: The delegation arrived to the airport late at night.
The delegation arrived at the airport late at night.
The delegation arrived at the airport late in night.
The delegation arrive at the airport late at night yesterday.
explanation: One arrives “at” a building or point (and “in” a city or country), never “to”.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “Each of the four provinces have its own high court.”
o: Each of the four provinces has its own high court.
Each of the four province has its own high court.
Each of the four provinces has their own high court.
Each of the four provinces have its own high court.
explanation: “Each” is singular, so it takes “has” and “its”; “each of the” is followed by a plural noun.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “The scheme is designed both to reduce poverty and for creating jobs.”
o: The scheme is designed both to reduce poverty and for creating jobs.
The scheme are designed both to reduce poverty and to create jobs.
The scheme is designed both to reduce poverty and to create jobs.
The scheme is designed both to reduce poverty as well as to create jobs.
explanation: “Both…and” must join parallel forms (two infinitives); “both” pairs with “and”, not “as well as”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “Ten years passed since he left the village.”?
o: Ten years passed since he left the village.
Ten years have passed since he left the village.
Ten years have passed from he left the village.
Ten years have passed since he has left the village.
explanation: With “since”, the main clause takes the present perfect (“have passed”) and the “since” clause takes the simple past.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “He paid with an one-rupee coin.”?
o: He paid with an one-rupee coin.
He paid by a one-rupee coin.
He paid with a one-rupees coin.
He paid with a one-rupee coin.
explanation: “One” begins with a “w” sound, so it takes “a”; compound adjectives such as “one-rupee” are not pluralised.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “The two neighbours have not spoken to one other for years.”
o: The two neighbours have not spoken to each other since years.
The two neighbours have not spoken to each other for years.
The two neighbours have not spoken to one other for years.
The two neighbours has not spoken to each other for years.
explanation: The reciprocal pronoun is “each other” (or “one another”); “for” is used with a period of time.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “The informations given in the brochure are outdated.”
o: The information giving in the brochure is outdated.
The information given in the brochure are outdated.
The information given in the brochure is outdated.
The informations given in the brochure are outdated.
explanation: “Information” is uncountable: no plural form and a singular verb.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “My grandfather use to walk five miles to school every day.”?
o: My grandfather used to walk five miles to school every day.
My grandfather use to walk five miles to school every day.
My grandfather used to walked five miles to school every day.
My grandfather used to walk five mile to school every day.
explanation: A past habit is expressed with “used to” + base verb.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The central bank should be independent from political pressure.”?
o: The central bank should be independent of politically pressure.
The central bank should is independent of political pressure.
The central bank should be independence of political pressure.
The central bank should be independent of political pressure.
explanation: Formal usage is “independent of”; after “should” the base form “be” is needed, and a noun is modified by an adjective.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “If the dam was to break, several villages will be flooded.”
o: If the dam were to break, several villages would flooded.
If the dam were to break, several villages would be flooded.
If the dam was to break, several villages will be flooded.
If the dam were to broke, several villages would be flooded.
explanation: A hypothetical future (“were to”) is paired with “would” in the main clause; “would be flooded” is the passive form.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “The new plant produces twice more electricity as the old one.”
o: The new plant produces twice as much electricity as the old one.
The new plant produces twice as many electricity as the old one.
The new plant produces twice more electricity as the old one.
The new plant produce twice as much electricity as the old one.
explanation: Multiples are expressed with “twice as much…as”; “electricity” is uncountable and takes “much”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “Passengers must keep their luggages with them at all times.”?
o: Passengers must keep there luggage with them at all times.
Passengers must keep their luggages with them at all times.
Passengers must keep their luggage with them at all times.
Passengers must keeps their luggage with them at all times.
explanation: “Luggage” is uncountable and has no plural form.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “Many retired officers enjoy to write about their careers.”?
o: Many retired officers enjoy to write about their careers.
Many retired officers enjoys writing about their careers.
Many retired officer enjoy writing about their careers.
Many retired officers enjoy writing about their careers.
explanation: “Enjoy” is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “The meeting is at ten o’clock, doesn’t it?”
o: The meeting is at ten o’clock, doesn’t it?
The meeting is on ten o’clock, isn’t it?
The meeting is at ten o’clock, wasn’t it?
The meeting is at ten o’clock, isn’t it?
explanation: A positive statement with “is” takes the negative tag “isn’t it?”; clock times take “at”.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “Thousands of people died with cholera and hunger in the famine of that year.”
o: Thousands of peoples died of cholera and hunger in the famine of that year.
Thousands of people died of cholera and hunger in the famine of that year.
Thousands of people died of cholera and hunger in famine of that year.
Thousands of people dies of cholera and hunger in the famine of that year.
explanation: The traditional collocation is “die of” a disease or hunger; the others contain agreement, article and plural errors.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “The director and myself will attend the conference in Geneva.”?
o: The director and I will attend the conference in Geneva.
The director and myself will attend the conference in Geneva.
The director and I will attending the conference in Geneva.
The director and me will attend the conference in Geneva.
explanation: A reflexive pronoun cannot be a subject; the subject pronoun is “I”.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The rich is not always happier than the poor.”?
o: The rich are not always more happier than the poor.
The rich is not always happier than the poor.
The rich are not always happier than the poor.
The riches are not always happier than the poor.
explanation: “The rich” refers to rich people as a group and is plural.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “The minister has left the building just now.”
o: The minister leaved the building just now.
The minister left the building just now.
The minister has left the building just now.
The minister left from the building just now.
explanation: “Just now” refers to a finished moment in the past and takes the simple past (whereas “just” alone goes with the present perfect).

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.”
o: The sun rise in the east and sets in the west.
Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
The sun rises from the east and sets in the west.
explanation: Unique objects such as the sun take “the”; the singular subject takes “rises”, and the direction takes “in the east”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “The board preferred to cut costs rather than raising prices.”?
o: The board preferred to cut costs rather than raise prices.
The board preferred to cut cost rather than raise prices.
The board prefer to cut costs rather than raise prices last year.
The board preferred to cut costs rather than raising prices.
explanation: Items joined by “rather than” should be parallel: “to cut…rather than (to) raise”.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The equipments in the laboratory needs to be replaced.”?
o: The equipments in the laboratory needs to be replaced.
The equipment in the laboratory need to be replaced.
The equipment in the laboratory needs to replaced.
The equipment in the laboratory needs to be replaced.
explanation: “Equipment” is uncountable, so it has no plural and takes the singular “needs”.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “She has always been good in mathematics and statistics.”
o: She has always been well at mathematics and statistics.
She has always been good at the mathematics and statistics.
She have always been good at mathematics and statistics.
She has always been good at mathematics and statistics.
explanation: The idiom is “good at” a subject; the others contain an agreement error, the adverb “well”, or an unnecessary article.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “Walk carefully lest you will slip on the wet floor.”
o: Walk carefully lest you should not slip on the wet floor.
Walk carefully lest you will slip on the wet floor.
Walk carefully lest you should slip on the wet floor.
Walk carefully lest you should slipped on the wet floor.
explanation: “Lest” is followed by “should” + base verb (or the bare subjunctive) and is already negative in meaning, so “not” is wrong.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “Of the two proposals, the second is the best.”?
o: Of the two proposals, the second is the better.
Of the two proposals, the second is the best.
Of the two proposals, the second is the more better.
Of the two proposal, the second is the better.
explanation: When only two things are compared, the comparative (“the better”) is used, not the superlative.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “After he finished his lecture, he had answered questions.”?
o: After he had finished his lecture, he answer questions.
After he had finished his lecture, he answered questions.
After he had finished his lecture, he answered to questions.
After he finished his lecture, he had answered questions.
explanation: The earlier action (finishing the lecture) takes the past perfect and the later one the simple past; “answer” takes a direct object.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “None of the work were completed before the deadline.”
o: None of the work was completed before the deadline.
None of the work was completed before the deadline expire.
None of the work were completed before the deadline.
None of the work was completing before the deadline.
explanation: With “none of”, the verb follows the noun: “work” is uncountable, so “was” is correct.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “The man which helped us has left the city.”
o: The man which helped us has left the city.
The man who helped us have left the city.
The man who helped us has left the city.
The man who helped we has left the city.
explanation: “Who” refers to people and “which” to things.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “The contractor is responsible of the delay in construction.”?
o: The contractor are responsible for the delay in construction.
The contractor is responsible of the delay in construction.
The contractor is responsibly for the delay in construction.
The contractor is responsible for the delay in construction.
explanation: The adjective “responsible” takes “for”.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The passengers objected to be searched without a reason.”?
o: The passengers objected to being search without a reason.
The passengers objected to being searched without a reason.
The passengers objected to be searched without a reason.
The passengers objected being searched without a reason.
explanation: In “object to”, “to” is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund (“being searched”).

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “No one never told us that the road was closed.”
o: No one ever telled us that the road was closed.
No one ever told us that the road was closed.
No one never told us that the road was closed.
No one ever told we that the road was closed.
explanation: “No one” is already negative, so “ever” rather than “never” must follow.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “Boys in the village play the cricket every evening.”
o: Boys in the village play the cricket every evening.
Boys in the village plays cricket every evening.
Boys in the village play cricket every evening.
Boys in the village play cricket every evenings.
explanation: Names of games take no article.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “I will call you when I will reach Islamabad.”?
o: I will call you when I reach Islamabad.
I will call you when I reached Islamabad.
I will call you when I will reach Islamabad.
I will call you when I reach to Islamabad.
explanation: Time clauses about the future use the present tense after “when”; “reach” takes a direct object.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “A series of lectures on climate change were organised by the university.”?
o: A series of lectures on climate change was organise by the university.
A series of lecture on climate change was organised by the university.
A series of lectures on climate change were organised by the university.
A series of lectures on climate change was organised by the university.
explanation: “A series” is singular, so the verb is “was”; the “of” phrase does not change the number.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “The auditor insisted for seeing the original receipts.”
o: The auditor insisted on seeing the original receipts.
The auditor insisted for seeing the original receipts.
The auditor insisted on to see the original receipts.
The auditor insist on seeing the original receipts yesterday.
explanation: “Insist” takes “on” followed by a gerund.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “Everyone except he was present at the meeting.”
o: Everyone except him were present at the meeting.
Everyone except he was present at the meeting.
Everyone except him was present at the meeting.
Every one except him was presents at the meeting.
explanation: “Except” is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun “him”; “everyone” is singular.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “Salman is so tall as his father.”?
o: Salman is as taller as his father.
Salman is as tall as his father.
Salman is so tall as his father.
Salman is as tall like his father.
explanation: An affirmative comparison of equality uses “as…as” with the positive adjective.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “The reason he resigned was because he disagreed with the policy.”?
o: The reason he resigned was that he disagree with the policy.
The reason he resigned was because he disagreed with the policy.
The reason he resigned were that he disagreed with the policy.
The reason he resigned was that he disagreed with the policy.
explanation: “The reason…is/was” is completed by “that”; “because” repeats the idea of reason.

subject: English
q: Choose the grammatically correct version of: “While we were having dinner, the guests arrive.”
o: While we were having dinner, the guests arrive.
While we was having dinner, the guests arrived.
While we were having dinner, the guests arrived.
While we were having dinner, the guests have arrived.
explanation: The main clause must stay in the past (“arrived”) to match the past continuous “were having”.

subject: English
q: Pick the correct form of the following sentence: “Measles are spreading in several districts after the floods.”
o: Measles is spreading in several districts after the floods.
Measles are spreading in several districts after the floods.
Measles is spreading in several district after the floods.
Measles is spreading in several districts since the floods.
explanation: Names of diseases ending in -s, such as “measles”, are singular.

subject: English
q: Which of the following correctly rewrites: “Several members abstained to vote on the resolution.”?
o: Several members abstained from vote on the resolution.
Several members abstained from voting on the resolution.
Several member abstained from voting on the resolution.
Several members abstained to vote on the resolution.
explanation: “Abstain” takes “from” followed by a gerund.

subject: English
q: Which option corrects the error in: “He is one of those officers who has never taken a bribe.”?
o: He is one of those officers who has never taken a bribe.
He is one of those officer who have never taken a bribe.
He is one of those officers who have never took a bribe.
He is one of those officers who have never taken a bribe.
explanation: In “one of those who”, the relative pronoun refers to the plural “officers”, so the verb is plural (“have”).
